title: Daily Operator Trust Pass
lede: Two small safeguards for the actions operators repeat all day, plus a second-pass fix that keeps rapid copy feedback truthful.

stats.n: Confirmation names the user and the cleanup consequences
Success follows a resolved write; failure leaves a manual-copy path
Older promises and timers cannot overwrite the newest attempt

sections.heading: Side by side
sections.note: The user-status pair uses the same authenticated admin, user, and viewport with its pre-change capture from clean HEAD. The copy pair is a timed interaction proof on the same authenticated guide and viewport.

pairs.title: User status action
pairs.sub: The Admin actions menu now pauses before a destructive status change.
pairs.beforeCap: Before: Deactivate user was the next click and had no consequence summary.
pairs.afterCap: After: the named user, sign-out, future-cancellation, and open-checkout constraint are visible before confirmation.

pairs.title: Repeated guide copy
pairs.sub: A second copy 900 ms after the first must receive its own complete 1.4-second feedback window.
pairs.beforeCap: Resting state: the table reference is ready to copy.
pairs.afterCap: 650 ms after the second click: Copied is still visible. The superseded first timer would already have fired 150 ms before this capture.

changes.h: Destructive status changes now explain their cost
changes.was: The operator could select Deactivate user and immediately start the cleanup mutation without a second look at who would be affected.
changes.now: The existing mutation waits behind the shared danger confirmation. Cancel closes the prompt without changing status; confirm keeps the existing server-side custody, cleanup, permission, and audit behavior.

changes.h: Copy actions now tell the truth
changes.was: Selected copy controls relied on direct browser writes, so denied or unavailable clipboard access could leave the operator without a useful outcome or recovery instruction.
changes.now: A shared helper reports success only after the browser write resolves. Failure shows a short manual-copy instruction while the visible value remains available across kiosk codes, guide references, calendar feeds, and item identity controls.

changes.h: Rapid repeats no longer shorten or scramble feedback
changes.was: Every successful item or guide copy started an independent timer. A first timer could clear a later success early, and a slow older clipboard result could replace the latest clicked identity value.
changes.now: The latest attempt owns the visible copied state. A repeat success cancels the older timer and receives the full display window; superseded promises are ignored and timers are cleared when the control leaves the page.

verification: Focused Vitest: 5 files and 24 tests passed, including clipboard rejection/unavailable-API behavior, latest-attempt wiring, Markdown, user, and item-link contracts.
TypeScript, lint, and app build: npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false, full npm run lint, and npm run build:app passed.

Authenticated local browser: the repeat-copy sequence held Copied 650 ms after the second click and reset afterward; the page had meaningful content, no framework overlay, and no warning/error logs. Prior confirmation proof still covers rendering, cancel-without-PATCH, and the controlled no-database confirm path.
Diff and docs hygiene: git diff --check passed. npm run verify:docs is blocked by generated architecture/frontend codemap drift in already-modified shared files, which this slice did not overwrite.
notes: This is a local Preview-backed review. No production deployment or production acceptance is claimed, and the browser confirmation apply used a fetch stub so no user record was changed.

The exact Kiosk Devices and Item identity click paths were source-wired, focused-tested, type-checked, linted, and compiled, but their populated browser states were not available as separate runtime captures in this pass.
